paragraphs: Forerunner sells software it calls a geospatial intelligence layer. The platform unifies geospatial data, field operations, and AI-powered workflows in one place. Local government is a core buyer, with compliance work across stormwater, floodplain, and code enforcement programs. The company also markets to energy and infrastructure operators handling inspections across active sites and assets.

At the base sits a map-first view holding every asset, permit parcel, violation, and environmental layer. On top of it run configurable workflows for inspections, permits, violations, and grant tracking. Inspection findings then generate corrective actions, and permit deadlines trigger notifications. The company says adoption brings no rip-and-replace projects and no major workflow disruptions. It claims teams are up and running in weeks.

Published case studies name the Puerto Rico Planning Board, which the company says replaced paper forms and spreadsheets for field inspections and code compliance. Another states that Lee County saves approximately 16 hours of staff time per week. A further case study describes Ponce Inlet centralizing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System workflows to reclaim 10 or more hours per week.
